site: RIKEN Center for Computational Science (R-CCS), Kobe
status: In service. Written from the operator's manual (portal.roquo.qc.r-ccs.riken.jp/manual/en), then checked against the live system on 2026-10-27. Verified live: SSH to login3, Slurm 26.05.3, both partitions and their node counts, the per-partition AllowQos and per-QOS MaxWall policy, get_resources, and that a rendered script is accepted and size-adjusted by sbatch. NOT verified: a job running to completion - the available project (qc-prj-tup0000) has zero billing points, so submission stops at ROQUO-E201. Where the manual and the live system disagreed, the values here follow the live system and say so.

login.key_registration: ROQUO Portal -> SSH Keys -> paste the contents of your .pub file -> Add. If the screen says keys cannot be changed there, open a portal ticket instead.
login.architecture_note: Login nodes are x86_64 but compute nodes are aarch64, so anything built on a login node will not run on a compute node. Build on a compute node.

partitions.name: roquo
partitions.description: Default partition; GB200 GPU compute nodes, aarch64. 135 nodes across 8 racks (qr01-qr08), node names like qr01n01.
partitions.max_nodes_per_job: No partition or normal-QOS cap (live: partition MaxNodes=UNLIMITED). The manual's '36 nodes per job' is the `general` QOS's MaxNodesPerJob, and `general` is not in this partition's AllowQos.

partitions.name: work
partitions.description: CPU-only partition, x86_64. Five nodes (work01-work05) for builds, pre/post-processing, workflow servers and VS Code Remote. No GPUs.
partitions.cpu: AMD EPYC 9655, 96 cores x 2 SMT threads = 192 logical CPUs per node

removed_partitions.note: Per-rack partitions were removed on 2026-10-13. Use --switches=1 on the roquo partition to keep an allocation inside one rack instead.

scheduler.account_note: Always set it. It selects both the billing target and the group that owns files the job writes; without it a job falls back to a restrictive default account. It is not a hard rejection, so a job can run and behave oddly instead of failing cleanly. List your accounts with `sacctmgr -nP show assoc user=$USER format=Account` or get_projects. get_projects returns both a billing group and an unchargeable personal account named after the username; only the former can be charged (ROQUO-E202). Billing is by points, and a job is refused up front if the group's balance is short (ROQUO-E201) - roughly 7000 points for a 5-minute single-GPU job and 66 for a 5-minute 2-CPU work job, as measured.

qos.note: Pass as custom_attributes.qos, which renders as #SBATCH --qos=<name>. Allowed-per-partition comes from `scontrol show partition` AllowQos; ceilings from `sacctmgr show qos` MaxWall. Verified live 2026-10-27.

max_wall.p4: no MaxWall set; bounded only by the partition's MaxTime
max_wall.p5: no MaxWall set; bounded only by the partition's MaxTime

other_limits.long: 4 CPUs and 8 GiB per job, 8 CPUs and 16 GiB per user, 4 concurrent jobs
other_limits.general: MaxWall 1 day, 36 nodes per job - but not in either partition's AllowQos, so unusable on roquo or work

qos.silent_trap: Exceeding a QOS's MaxWall while still inside the partition's MaxTime is accepted by Slurm and then never scheduled: the job parks on QOSMaxWallDurationPerJobLimit, which looks identical to a busy queue. This is any work job over 3 days without --qos=long, and equally any roquo job over its p1/p2/p3 ceiling. submit_job refuses these up front.

node_plans.note: A GPU request on the roquo partition rounds up to one of three fixed plans. Asking for more than one full node's worth in a single --gres request is rejected with ROQUO-E001; use --gres=gpu:4 with --nodes=N instead.
node_plans.default_plan: qtr (what a job with no GPU, CPU or memory flags receives)

scheduler.topology: Add --switches=1 to keep an allocation within one rack. It waits up to 5 minutes before spanning racks; --switches=1@<time> shortens that wait.

error_codes.ROQUO-E001: GPU/CPU/memory request exceeds one node. Use --gres=gpu:4 --nodes=N.
error_codes.ROQUO-E101: No CPU count given on the work partition. Set --cpus-per-task or --ntasks.
error_codes.ROQUO-E102: Too many CPUs requested on work (max 192).
error_codes.ROQUO-E103: Too much memory requested on work (max 8 GiB per allocated CPU).
error_codes.ROQUO-W003: Not an error despite the prefix: ROQUO prints warnings as 'sbatch: error: [ROQUO-Wnnn]'. W003 means the request was rounded up to a node plan (e.g. to the 1/4 slot: 1 GPU / 36 cores / 400000 MB), which is normal. Judge success by sbatch's exit status and whether a job id came back, not by the presence of 'error:' in its output.
error_codes.ROQUO-E201: Insufficient billing points for the charging group: 'Not enough billing points (remaining N, this job needs M). Billing group: <project>.' The job is refused and sbatch ends with the unhelpful 'Batch job submission failed: Unspecified error', so read the whole stderr, not just the last line. There is no CLI for the balance - it is in the ROQUO Portal - and the fix is to ask the administrators to add points, or to charge a different project with attributes.account.
error_codes.ROQUO-E202: A job was submitted against a personal account: 'Jobs cannot be submitted with a personal account (<username>).' sacctmgr lists a personal association alongside the real billing group, and it is not chargeable. get_projects marks each entry with chargeable true/false so this is visible before submitting. Use the qc-prj-* billing group.

scheduler.mail_note: Notifications need both --mail-type (e.g. END,FAIL) and --mail-user set to a full address containing '@'. A bare username silently sends nothing.
scheduler.output_note: sbatch messages are bilingual: each line appears in Japanese and then in English. Both lines carry the same ROQUO-nnn code, so match on the code rather than on message text.

compute_node.interconnect: One NIC directly attached per GPU, GPUDirect RDMA enabled.
compute_node.measured_bandwidth: ~93 GB/s for a single GPU pair at 16 MB; ~378 GB/s aggregate across two nodes of 4 GPUs at 32 MB

home.purpose: Small area for configuration and source. Not for datasets or images.
home.quota: not published in the manual (listed as TBD) - read it live

project.purpose: Persistent, shared by project members. Datasets, results and container (SIF) images belong here.
project.quota: not published in the manual (listed as TBD) - read it live; changes are requested through the portal with a required reason

scratch.purged: deleted when the job ends - copy anything you need out before then
scratch.tmpdir_note: $TMPDIR points at $SLURM_SCRATCH/tmp inside a job. Do not write to /tmp directly.

modules.login_node_note: Modules load on compute nodes only, not on login nodes. A module load in a login shell will not behave like one inside a job.

available.name: cuda/13.3
available.description: CUDA Toolkit. Note `module load cuda` resolves to cuda/13.4, which is the default, not 13.3.

available.name: hpcx/2.50
available.description: NVIDIA HPC-X, OpenMPI 5 over UCX. Launch with srun (PMIx). hpcx/2.51 is also available.

available.name: nvhpc-openmpi/26.5
available.description: HPC-X bundled with NVHPC, OpenMPI 4 over UCX. Launch with mpirun, not srun.

mpi.mutually_exclusive: Lmod swaps one stack out when the other is loaded - they cannot both be active.
gotchas: On the NVHPC stack, `srun --mpi=pmix` aborts before MPI_Init and is unsupported. Use mpirun.
Do not load the cuda module or set NVHPC_CUDA_HOME alongside the NVHPC stack; it breaks mpirun.
Plain -lmpi fails with 'cannot find -lmpi'. Pass the MPI include and library paths explicitly.
mpicc -cuda does not work (a CUDA 13.2 device-header conflict). Compile with nvcc using nvc++ as host compiler, or call nvc++ directly.
Call cudaSetDevice() and cudaFree(0) before MPI_Init, or the job aborts with 'cannot find remote protocol'.
Slurm's TaskProlog injects the UCX settings CUDA-aware MPI needs. Do not unset them.
NVSHMEM applications (e.g. HPL in the hpc-benchmarks container) need NVSHMEM_IBGDA_NIC_HANDLER=cpu_host_memory, or they can hang after cuda_nvshmem_init. Plain CUDA-aware MPI does not need it.
Request whole nodes (--gres=gpu:4) for tightly coupled multi-node work: fewer GPUs means fewer NICs and less bandwidth.

containers.architecture_note: Images must be aarch64-compatible. An x86_64 image will not run on a compute node.

vscode_remote.note: You can only SSH into a work node while your own job is running on it. The documented approach puts a ProxyCommand in your local ~/.ssh/config that runs srun on the login node and relays through socat to the node's sshd, so VS Code allocates a node on connect and releases it on disconnect. socat is preinstalled on work nodes. The connection drops when --time expires.
